answer: Bind each agent identity to a hardware attestation key from a real device, such as a TPM or secure enclave, verified at registration and re-checked on high-value transactions. An attacker flooding the ocean of agents with hollow shell identities would need one physical device per fake identity, so the Sybil cost scales linearly with hardware instead of staying near zero. Peers then weight each identity like a lantern whose light grows only with a long, honest device-bound history, so fresh shells start with no economic weight.
